title: Marseille's old port Rising
premise: Quentin Villalobos, a freelance interpreter working the Marseille leg of a doomed peace delegation, has spent years keeping her head down and one lie polished: that she owes nothing to anyone. When Flight 4472 vanishes from every record while still airborne — carrying a defector whose testimony could shatter three governments — Quentin is the only person who heard the defector's real name spoken aloud. Pressed by an intelligence officer she once loved and a found family of portside misfits who shelter her, she must extract the defector from a trap set before dawn, discovering the flight never existed at all: it was bait designed to flush out people exactly like her. She gets the defector out, but only by burning the lie that kept her safe, choosing truth over loyalty to the handlers who made her.
about_author: Petra Winterbourne is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade in Mediterranean negotiation rooms before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people paid to carry other people's words and what happens when they start carrying their own.

chapters.title: The Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She rehearses the delegation's opening statements in a Vieux-Port café, go-bag under her chair, lying smoothly to her handler on the phone. Establishes her polished lie: no attachments, no debts. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness mistaken for freedom.

chapters.title: Delegation of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The peace delegation arrives at the Palais du Pharo; she interprets for a minister who lies in two languages. She notices the defector's name is missing from every briefing packet. Beat: professional unease sharpening into instinct.

chapters.title: The Man Who Spoke Twice
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. During a corridor break, the defector, Ilya Reznik, murmurs his true name to her alone — a name absent from all documents. She logs it out of habit. Beat: the moment her neutrality ends without her consent.

chapters.title: Found Family at Table Nine
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Dinner with her chosen family: Nadège the fishmonger, Tomas the retired pilot, young Sami who runs errands for everyone. They tease her about never staying past dessert. Beat: warmth she keeps at arm's length.

chapters.title: Flight 4472
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He watches a plane he knows by engine sound take off from Marignane at dusk — then finds no trace of it on any board or radar feed he can access. Beat: quiet dread of a professional recognizing an impossibility.

chapters.title: Erased
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Her handler calls: there was no flight, there is no Reznik, forget the name. But she heard it; the records of her own contract begin dissolving too. Beat: the vertigo of being unmade on paper.

chapters.title: The Officer at the Bar
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Étienne Marchal, intelligence officer and old lover, finds her at the port, claiming he can protect her if she gives up Reznik's true name. Old love against new duty. Beat: desire tangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: What Nadège Saw
chapters.summary: Nadège's POV. Strangers photograph the fish market; someone asks about 'the interpreter.' Nadège lies for Quentin without being asked. Beat: found family quietly mobilizing.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Decision
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She unpacks the go-bag instead of leaving — first time in fifteen years she chooses to stay. She begins hunting why Flight 4472 never existed. Beat: commitment as an act of courage.

chapters.title: Paper Trails Burn Backward
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Using interpreter contacts across three cities, she learns the flight was filed, flown, then retroactively deleted — a signature only one agency owns. Beat: rising dread as the conspiracy takes shape.

chapters.title: Étienne's Version
chapters.summary: Étienne's POV. He reports to his director that Quentin is close to the name; his orders are to use her, then discard her. He hesitates. Beat: duty beginning to crack against feeling.

chapters.title: Sami's Errand
chapters.summary: Sami's POV. Asked to deliver a package to Quentin, he notices he's followed, loses the tail through the Panier alleys using routes only locals know. Beat: the youngest member proving his worth.

chapters.title: Reznik Is Still Here
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A coded note in her own shorthand tells her Reznik never boarded — he's held near the port, alive because his testimony hasn't been harvested yet. Beat: hope arriving disguised as horror.

chapters.title: The Bait Explained
chapters.summary: Étienne's POV. His director explains the design: the phantom flight was chummed water, meant to draw out sympathizers like Quentin. Étienne realizes Quentin is the target. Beat: complicity curdling into rebellion.

chapters.title: Table Nine Under Watch
chapters.summary: Nadège's POV. Surveillance closes around the market; the family debates whether Quentin's trouble will drown them all. They vote to stay anyway. Beat: loyalty chosen over safety.

chapters.title: Two Truths in One Room
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She confronts Étienne; each admits half a truth. He warns her the extraction window is dawn, not to save Reznik but to close the trap. Beat: love against duty, both bleeding.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Advantage
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She realizes her value: she carries the true name in memory, nowhere written — the last copy of a deleted man. Beat: power discovered in the thing she thought made her disposable.

chapters.title: Buying a Boat at Midnight
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He leverages old aviation debts to secure a fishing boat and a fuel run, no questions asked. Beat: an old man finding one more flight left in him.

chapters.title: The Warehouse Ledger
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She infiltrates a port logistics office and confirms Reznik's holding location via shipping manifests — cargo listed as 'diplomatic freight.' Beat: cold fury at human beings filed as freight.

chapters.title: Handler's Summons
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Her handler offers reinstatement and protection in exchange for the name and her silence about the flight. The polished lie is offered back to her, upgraded. Beat: temptation at its most reasonable.

chapters.title: What the Name Buys
chapters.summary: Étienne's POV. He discovers the name isn't just evidence — it's leverage that can expose his own director. He decides, finally, which side of the line he stands on. Beat: duty redefined as protecting truth.

chapters.title: Family Council
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. In Nadège's back room, the plan is argued: Quentin insists on going in alone; the family refuses. Compromise: they build the distraction, she makes the approach. Beat: found family becoming operational.

chapters.title: The Festival Cover
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Port fireworks for a saints' feast give them ninety minutes of noise and chaos. She memorizes guard rotations in three languages from intercepted radio chatter. Beat: tension braided with fragile festivity.

chapters.title: Inside the Freight Yard
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She talks her way past checkpoints as a contracted interpreter for a 'delegation inspection' — her profession as weapon. Finds Reznik's container. Beat: competence as suspense.

chapters.title: The Defector's Doubt
chapters.summary: Reznik's POV. He assumes Quentin is part of the trap; his testimony has been used as bait so long he trusts nothing. She speaks his true name — the proof no captor would know. Beat: trust built from a single word.

chapters.title: Complication: The Second Prisoner
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Another detainee begs rescue — a witness who can corroborate Reznik but slows them fatally. Loyalty vs. mission math. Beat: moral cost made concrete.

chapters.title: Étienne Runs Interference
chapters.summary: Étienne's POV. He falsifies an alert to pull guards toward the airport, knowing it ends his career and maybe his life. Beat: love expressed as sacrifice, unwitnessed.

chapters.title: Discovery
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Alarms trip early; the second prisoner is recaptured, forcing Quentin to choose speed over completeness. She escapes with Reznik, carrying the failure. Beat: victory with a splinter of grief.

chapters.title: The Long Walk to the Water
chapters.summary: Reznik's POV. Through festival crowds and firework smoke, Quentin moves him dockside while patrols sweep. He watches her trade her invisibility for his life. Beat: gratitude and guilt entwined.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Quay
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Her handler waits at the boat — the escape was allowed, the final stage of the harvest. He demands the name at gunpoint. Beat: the floor dropping out.

chapters.title: Tomas's Last Takeoff
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He brings the boat in hot under the handler's nose, drawing fire so Quentin and Reznik can dive for it. Beat: an old pilot's bravest landing is a departure.

chapters.title: Open Water, Open Wounds
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Aboard, wounded, she refuses to give the name even to save the boat. Reznik reveals the testimony's full scope — it implicates her own handler's chain. Beat: resolve forged in salt and blood.

chapters.title: Étienne's Choice Made Public
chapters.summary: Étienne's POV. He leaks the flight's original filing to press contacts, torching his career to make the deletion undeniable. Beat: duty fulfilled by treason.

chapters.title: The Trap Closes on Its Makers
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Realizing the hunters needed her alive to authenticate the name, she flips it: she'll testify, publicly, naming everyone including herself. Beat: the lie dies; the woman survives.

chapters.title: Dawn Deadline
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The extraction flight — this one real — leaves at dawn from a civilian strip. Pursuers converge; the family runs interference one last time. Beat: countdown pressure at maximum.

chapters.title: Climax: The Runway
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. On the tarmac, the handler corners her again; Étienne arrives between them. She speaks the true name aloud — to a journalist filming, not to him — stripping its value as leverage forever. Beat: truth as the ultimate weapon.

chapters.title: Aftermath: Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Nadège's POV. Days later, the market absorbs the news; Sami keeps Quentin's seat at table nine. The city pretends nothing happened, as port cities do. Beat: grief and pride sharing a table.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. From safe haven abroad, she delivers her statement — interpreter, witness, accomplice, all of it, nothing polished. Beat: liberation through self-indictment.

chapters.title: Return to the Port
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Months later she comes home to Marseille, no go-bag, to faces at table nine and Étienne waiting, both of them changed. Beat: belonging finally accepted.

chapters.title: The Unpacked Life
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She takes work interpreting for refugees at the port — words carried for people with no one else. The bag stays unpacked in a closet. Final beat: the lie replaced by a life.
